name: Spector Frame Inspector
description: GENEX-owned MCP bridge to the official Spector.js WebGL debugger server built and installed locally. Localhost-first frame forensics.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Inspect configured upstream entry path and SHA-256 lock. Does not start a browser or prove the MCP server is ready.

tools.name: probe
tools.description: Launch the exact SHA-256-reviewed upstream through the existing MCP proxy, complete a bounded MCP initialize/tools-list handshake, and report actual discovered tool availability. No website navigation; not gameplay proof.
tools.confirmation: Start the locally configured upstream MCP server for a 12-second handshake check? This executes trusted local Node code and may start a browser service.

skills.name: webgl-frame-forensics
skills.summary: Use official Spector.js MCP frame capture to inspect local WebGL games; read setup, supported captures and limitations before agent use.

settings.label: Reviewed upstream entry script SHA-256 (64 hex characters)
Exact local game origin (scheme, host, port)

actions.name: probe
actions.label: Test MCP connection
actions.confirmation: Start the locally configured Spector MCP server to test its protocol and tools? It executes native local code.

mcpServers.description: Runs the local built Spector.js MCP server inside Node. Direct load_url calls must match the configured game origin, but browser page requests/redirects are not a complete sandbox. Requires separately building BabylonJS/Spector.js/mcp, installing its browser dependency and setting an absolute dist/index.js path. The entry script must match the configured SHA-256 digest. This does not pin transitive npm dependencies.
